ledger.hypothesis: this node is ELEMENTWISE (O(output), no second collection to scan), so there is no acceleration structure to build -- the levers are whole-array temporaries and per-evaluation work derived from an input that did not change. getVertexNormals re-averages 159602 normals every tick while only amplitude/frequency/speed/time animate, so caching it should dominate. dgdirty(node) re-marks the input geom plug every tick without changing a byte of it, so a setDependentsDirty/preEvaluation flag would invalidate on every evaluation and never hit; the cache has to be earned with the item-2 content fingerprint instead, folded into the centre pass that already holds every coordinate in a register.
ledger.risk: the fingerprint is the whole correctness argument. Normals are a pure function of (points, topology); every point is hashed BITWISE plus the vertex count and the geometry index, so a fresh upstream shape -- what the GEO parity path rewires per config -- moves points and misses. The residual hole is two meshes with byte-identical positions in identical order but different connectivity, which the harness does not generate. Second risk: the parallel map is a permitted deterministic per-element write, but the centre sum stays SERIAL on purpose -- reassociating a 159602-term reduction drifts ~1 ULP and would pass the tolerance gate while breaking byte parity.
ledger.theme: fuse the six whole-array nd:: temporaries into one per-vertex pass, then key a per-node vertex-normal cache on a bitwise fingerprint of the input points so a cache hit never calls outputArrayValue(input) at all
